page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 60 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The instance does not include integrated local storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated hardware GPUs are present.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded execution driven by the 3.9 GHz sustained clock frequency. The instance achieves strong scores in Geekbench single-core (2192.0), single-threaded gzip compression (34.63 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (14.54 GB/sec), alongside strong Geekbench text processing (2723.0). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU hardware footprint. Stress-ng multi-core testing (4318.97) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (27.67 GB/sec) score in the lower quartile, as do compilation benchmarks with Clang (5419.0). Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth registered at 36.01 GB/sec, while cached small-block read operations reached 353.92 GB/sec.

In evaluating resource trade-offs, the r7iz.xlarge prioritizes per-core memory capacity and high per-thread CPU performance over raw multi-core scaling. The inclusion of DDR5 memory and AMX instruction extensions enhances efficiency for targeted compute routines like small-scale machine learning inference, where the instance achieves 617.85 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 147.33 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M parameter model. The absence of local instance storage requires external network volumes for stateful persistence.

Workload fit centers on applications demanding high single-thread clock rates matched with generous memory allocations. It is well-aligned for memory-intensive backend services, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases that do not demand extensive parallel core counts, and small-model inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 6455B processor running at 3.9 GHz. It offers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and networking provides a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing reveals top-quartile single-core CPU execution, single-threaded compression performance, and text processing, while overall multi-threaded throughput remains bounded by the 4-vCPU size. With its combination of high per-core clocks and high RAM density, r7iz.xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that rely on single-thread speed, including EDA tooling, relational databases with moderate parallelism, and low-latency data processing tasks.
